name: Paperweight
use_label: Map your digital footprint from email
one_liner: A local-first app that scans your inbox to map where your data lives and where you've signed up.

text.why: Forgotten accounts and bulk mail pile up and it's hard to know where your data went. Paperweight reads your inbox to find accounts and mailing lists per service, and shows breach alerts and data-deletion requests.
text.take: The source is open, so you can audit what it does.
build: Works with Gmail, Microsoft, Apple, Proton (via Bridge) and IMAP. It finds accounts and mailing lists, shows breach alerts (haveibeenpwned.com) and offers bulk unsubscribe. It says mail and settings stay on your machine and nothing is sent to external servers; a scan takes about two minutes.

who.role: Anyone who wants to clean up old sign-ups and marketing mail.

start.text: Download the build for your OS from Releases, connect your email and run a scan.

caveat: The free tier covers one email account and discovery only. Unsubscribe and deletion actions, multiple accounts and MCP need a paid plan (a 30-day Cleanup Pass or yearly Pro). It reads your whole mailbox, so check the source and pricing before granting access.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
